title: Water Quality Management
description: Comprehensive standard operating procedure for maintaining optimal water quality in aquaculture systems. Covers daily parameter testing, equipment calibration, species-specific optimal ranges, and emergency response protocols for out-of-range conditions. Applicable across all organism types including coral, oyster, kelp, finfish, and seagrass.

steps.title: Safety First
steps.description: Before beginning water quality testing, ensure you are wearing appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE). Chemical reagents used in water testing can cause skin and eye irritation. Never taste or ingest any testing solutions.
checklistItems: Lab coat or protective clothing on

steps.title: Prepare Testing Equipment
steps.description: Gather all necessary testing equipment and ensure probes are properly calibrated. Inaccurate equipment leads to incorrect readings and poor management decisions. Check calibration dates on all meters and replace expired reagents.

steps.title: Equipment Calibration Verification
steps.description: Verify that all testing equipment has been calibrated within the required timeframe. Document any equipment requiring recalibration before proceeding with testing.
checklistItems: pH meter calibrated within last 24 hours using pH 4.0 and 7.0 buffers
Salinity refractometer zeroed with distilled water
Temperature probe verified against reference thermometer
Dissolved oxygen meter calibrated in air-saturated water
Ammonia test kit reagents within expiration date
Nitrate test kit reagents within expiration date
Alkalinity test kit reagents within expiration date

steps.title: Collect Water Samples
steps.description: Collect water samples from representative locations in each system. For large systems, collect samples from at least 3 locations: inlet, middle, and outlet. Use clean sampling containers rinsed with sample water before collection. Record exact sampling locations for consistency.

steps.title: Temperature Measurement
steps.description: Measure water temperature at each sampling location. Temperature affects all other water quality parameters and organism metabolism. Record both ambient air temperature and water temperature. Note any significant temperature stratification in deep systems.

steps.title: pH Measurement
steps.description: Measure pH using a calibrated meter. Rinse probe with sample water before measurement. Wait for reading to stabilize (typically 30-60 seconds). Record pH to one decimal place. pH affects nutrient availability and organism stress levels.

steps.title: Salinity Measurement
steps.description: Measure salinity using a refractometer or digital meter. For refractometers, apply 2-3 drops to the prism and read the scale against natural light. Salinity is critical for osmoregulation in all aquatic organisms.

steps.title: Dissolved Oxygen Measurement
steps.description: Measure dissolved oxygen (DO) using a calibrated DO meter. Submerge probe at least 10cm below surface and gently agitate to ensure accurate reading. Record in mg/L and % saturation. Low DO is one of the most immediate threats to organism health.

steps.title: Ammonia Testing
steps.description: Test for total ammonia nitrogen (TAN) using appropriate test kit or meter. Ammonia is highly toxic to aquatic organisms. Note: toxicity increases with higher pH and temperature. Calculate unionized ammonia (NH3) using provided conversion tables if TAN is elevated.

steps.title: Nitrate and Nitrite Testing
steps.description: Test nitrite (NO2) and nitrate (NO3) levels. Nitrite is toxic and indicates incomplete nitrification. Nitrate is less toxic but high levels indicate poor water exchange or overfeeding. Both parameters help assess biofilter performance.

steps.title: Optimal Parameter Ranges
steps.description: Reference optimal ranges for your specific organisms. General marine ranges: Temperature 24-28C (coral/tropical), 15-20C (temperate), pH 7.8-8.4, Salinity 32-36 ppt, DO >6mg/L (>80% saturation), Ammonia <0.02mg/L, Nitrite <0.1mg/L, Nitrate <20mg/L. Freshwater systems have different requirements. Always consult species-specific guidelines.

steps.title: Record All Results
steps.description: Document all test results in the daily log with timestamp, location, and operator initials. Compare against baseline and previous readings to identify trends.
checklistItems: Results entered into digital tracking system

steps.title: Emergency Response for Critical Values
steps.description: If any parameter is outside critical thresholds, initiate emergency response immediately. Critical thresholds: DO <4mg/L, pH <7.2 or >8.8, Ammonia >0.5mg/L, Temperature deviation >3C from normal. Notify supervisor immediately and begin corrective action.

steps.title: Corrective Actions for Low Dissolved Oxygen
steps.description: For low DO: Increase aeration immediately. Check air pump operation. Reduce feeding temporarily. Check for dead organisms. Consider partial water exchange with well-oxygenated water. Reduce stocking density if chronic issue.

steps.title: Corrective Actions for Ammonia Spike
steps.description: For elevated ammonia: Reduce or stop feeding immediately. Perform 25-50% water exchange with treated water. Check biofilter media and flow. Inspect for dead organisms. Add zeolite or ammonia-removing media if available. Increase monitoring to every 4 hours.

steps.title: Clean and Store Equipment
steps.description: After testing, rinse all probes with distilled water. Store pH probes in storage solution (never allow to dry). Return reagents to proper storage. Clean spills immediately. Dispose of used test samples appropriately.

steps.title: Daily Water Quality Completion Checklist
steps.description: Verify all daily water quality tasks have been completed before signing off.
checklistItems: All results recorded and entered digitally
Handoff notes completed for next shift
